perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'That he found was extraordinary.' The sentence needs a free relative supplying both the subject of 'was' and the missing object of transitive 'found': 'What he found was extraordinary.' Complementizer 'that' introduces a complete clause, but 'he found' lacks an object, so the that-clause is defective. Rescue readings fail: intransitive 'find' is archaic/biblical and contextually incoherent (the discourse is about what Bargh discovered); demonstrative 'That' cannot head a zero restrictive relative ('That [which] he found') in standard modern English — 'that which' or 'what' would be required. Ungrammatical as written.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: 'Those students who had been exposed ... took almost 40 percent longer to walk ...' — long-distance subject 'students' (plural) governs 'took'; simple past matches the narrative frame; past perfect in the relative clause correctly marks anteriority; 'take + duration + to-inf' is the licensed construction. Grammatical.

note: Classic What/That free-relative item. The error is unambiguous: 'found' is object-less, so only a fused relative 'What' can simultaneously satisfy the matrix subject slot and the embedded object slot. No alternative parse (reduced relative, inversion, intransitive find) renders (D) well-formed in this context. All other underlines are demonstrably grammatical, so the item has exactly one defensible key.
